judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is exactly as stated, and I checked it directly rather than inheriting it. final_response.md describes the three documents in prose — 'Worksheet — 8 problems', 'Answer key — step by step', 'Study guide — 2 pages, four sections' — and contains no filename, no path and no link for any of them. Every sibling case in this shard that passed the gate names its artifacts (curr-023 'ws_addstories_curr023.pdf', curr-034 'ws_teenplace_curr034.pdf', curr-045 'ws_measure_curr045.pdf', curr-062, curr-073 and curr-084 likewise), so this is a delivery regression in this one run, not a missing suite convention. The judge's countervailing claim is also correct: the packet itself is sound. I recomputed all eight items from the block pictures — 2/4/3 -> 243; 3/0/6 -> 306; 5/7/2 -> 572; 1/8/0 -> 180; six rods -> 60; 2 flats, 13 rods, 5 units traded -> 335; 342 > 328; 426 versus (300+120+9)=429 -> '<' — and found no error, including the trade in problem 8 that makes Rosa's flat-counting argument fail. REJECT on the delivery gate with the mathematics intact is the right call.

strengths_to_preserve: No figure on the sheet carries a printed numeral. The flat/rod/unit key is stated once in the directions and every model is drawn with \btmodel, so problem 6 (2 flats, 13 rods, 5 units) genuinely requires reading the picture — and no problem can borrow a neighbour's labelled value.

Problem 6's solution shows both routes and reconciles them: '13 rods = 1 flat + 3 rods' giving 300 + 30 + 5, then 'Check without trading: 200 + 130 + 5 = 335 — same number, as it must be.' That is the conservation argument the trade depends on, written out rather than assumed.

Problem 2 plants the zero-placeholder slip in the stem itself ('Careful — one place is empty here') and the key names the wrong answer explicitly: 'Writing 36 is the classic slip: it would mean 3 tens and 6 ones.'

Problem 8 is a well-built challenge: the trade must happen BEFORE the comparison, and after it both models have 4 hundreds and 2 tens so the ones decide — which is precisely why 'more flats on the table' was never the right test, and the key says so.

root_causes.description: The final response is written as a description of the work rather than as a delivery of it. Nothing in the pipeline binds the three compiled PDF paths that build.sh prints in its '-- PDFs --' block into final_response.md, so a run can pass all 22 gates, produce three correct PDFs, and still fail the delivery requirement — which is what happened here.
evidence: final_response.md: the three documents are named only as 'Worksheet', 'Answer key' and 'Study guide'; no filename, path or link appears anywhere in the file.

gate_log.txt does print the three artifact paths under its '-- PDFs --' block (ws_r_curr051.pdf, ak_r_curr051.pdf, ss_r_curr051.pdf), so the information the response needed was already computed by the build.

Sibling cases in the same run, from the same generator, name their files in prose (curr-023, curr-034, curr-045, curr-062, curr-073, curr-084), confirming the omission is a per-run lapse rather than a missing convention.
official_score.hard_failures lists all three artifacts as unsurfaced, dropping instruction_following from 4 to 1 while every other dimension scored 4.

root_causes.description: Six of the eight problems print more student-fillable slots than verify.json covers. Problems 1 and 2 print three place-value blanks each, problems 3 and 4 print a three-term expanded form each, and problems 7 and 8 print 'Model A = ___' and 'Model B = ___' before the comparison. In every case a single entry covers the last value only. On problems 3 and 4 the unverified part IS the declared skill: the entries are tagged 'expanded-form-from-model' and the expanded form itself is what goes unchecked.
evidence: worksheet.tex problems 1-2: '\underline{\hspace{1.2cm}} hundreds \quad \underline{\hspace{1.2cm}} tens \quad \underline{\hspace{1.2cm}} ones' — three slots; verify ids 1 and 2 hold one eval each (243, 306).

worksheet.tex problems 3-4: 'Expanded form: \underline{\hspace{1.4cm}} $+$ \underline{\hspace{1.4cm}} $+$ \underline{\hspace{1.4cm}}' — three slots; verify ids 3 and 4 hold one eval each (572, 180) and are tagged "skill": "expanded-form-from-model".

worksheet.tex problems 7-8: 'Model A $=$ \underline{\hspace{1.6cm}}' and 'Model B $=$ \underline{\hspace{1.6cm}}' plus the symbol blank; verify ids 7 and 8 hold one compare entry each, and answer_key.tex boxes only \ans{>} / \ans{<}, so the model values 342, 328, 426 and 429 are unboxed prose.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py resolves a string 'expected' by sympify+latex and falls back to a TeX em-dash when sympify raises. A bare relation symbol is not a sympifiable expression, so every compare problem whose order is 'relation' is silently banked as '---' — the marker the module documents as 'manual-only / see solution'. The verified answer exists and is correct; the grader's quick-reference column simply refuses to print it.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '1. 243  2. 306  3. 572  4. 180  5. 60  6. 335  7. -  8. -' — the two challenge problems are the two with no banked answer.
verify.json ids 7 and 8 are compare entries with "order": "relation" and expected '>' and '<'; gate_log.txt records both as PASS.

improvements.title: final_response.md must name and link the three delivered PDFs
improvements.proposed_change: Close the loop mechanically instead of by instruction. build.sh already collects the three output paths for its '-- PDFs --' block; have it write them to a small manifest (outdir/artifacts.txt, one path per line) at the end of a successful build, and state in SKILL.md's delivery step that the final response must name each of the three files from that manifest. Then add a delivery gate to tests/check_artifact_health.py: given a run directory, fail when final_response.md does not mention the worksheet, answer-key and study-guide filenames.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture run directory holding the three PDFs plus a final_response.md that describes them only in prose ('Worksheet — 8 problems.'): the delivery check must exit non-zero and name all three missing artifacts. A second fixture whose final_response.md contains the three filenames must exit 0. Seed the first fixture with curr-051's retained final_response.md verbatim so the test reproduces this exact failure. No such check exists today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Eliminates the class of REJECTs where the mathematics scored 4/4 on every dimension and the run still failed. This case lost 3 points and its verdict to it; the fix makes the failure impossible rather than merely documented.
improvements.risk: Low. The check reads a text file and looks for filenames. The one care point is that different runs use different stems (ws_r_curr051 versus ws_addstories_curr023), so the check must read the manifest build.sh wrote rather than assume a naming pattern.

improvements.title: Expanded-form and model-value blanks ship unverified on six of eight problems
improvements.proposed_change: Give each printed blank its own entry under the problem's id, using the multi-entry-per-id form: ids 1 and 2 gain evals for the hundreds/tens/ones digits, ids 3 and 4 gain evals for 500, 70, 2 and 100, 80, 0, and ids 7 and 8 gain evals for the two model values (342/328 and 426/429) alongside the existing compare — with the key boxing those values in \ans{} so the answer-key binding gate sees them. Systemically, add the printed-slot count gate to tests/check_layout.py described under this same issue_key in the curr-023 and curr-034 reviews.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 3 stem prints three \underline{\hspace{1.4cm}} slots for an expanded form, paired with a verify JSON holding one eval for that id: check_layout.py must exit 2 naming problem 3 as '3 printed slots, 1 verified'. With three entries under the id it must exit 0. Today the one-entry fixture exits 0.
improvements.expected_impact: On this sheet it converts six problems from partially verified to fully verified, and in particular makes the expanded form — the declared skill of problems 3 and 4 — a checked answer. It also gives the Quick Answers bank something to print for problems 7 and 8 beyond the relation symbol.
improvements.risk: Slot counting over LaTeX is heuristic and will over-count decorative rules; run it at exit 2 and reuse check_layout.py's existing per-block parser.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified relation symbol
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation strings in _fmt() BEFORE the sympify attempt: map '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=' (and the unicode forms) to '$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\ne$'. sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError, so today every compare entry with "order": "relation" drops into the '---' fallback that exists for genuinely unrenderable values. Keep '---' for manual-only ids and for real sympify failures, so the fallback still means 'see the worked solution'.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON of [{'id':1,'type':'compare','values':['3','7'],'order':'relation','expected':'<'}, {'id':2,'type':'compare','values':['9','4'],'order':'relation','expected':'>'}, {'id':3,'type':'manual','desc':'open'}] and asserts the bank lines are '$<$', '$>$' and '---' respectively. Today entries 1 and 2 both render '---', so the assertion fails; after the relation mapping it passes, and the manual id still prints '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the two comparison answers to a grading column that currently gives a teacher nothing at all for the sheet's two hardest problems — the ones where a quick reference is most useful.
improvements.risk: Low. Bank entries stay plain text (no \ans/\boxed), so check_answer_key.py's strict per-problem boxed-answer binding is untouched, and column_count() only sees a 3-char string. The only judgement call is math-mode wrapping of '='; both '=' and '$=$' set correctly inside the multicols block.

case_summary: A mathematically excellent base-ten packet rejected for delivery, and the rejection is correct: final_response.md describes the worksheet, key and study guide but names no file for any of them, while six sibling cases in the same run do. I recomputed all eight items — including the 13-rod trade in problem 6 and the 12-rod trade that breaks Rosa's argument in problem 8 — and found no error. Two further gaps the judge did not reach: six of eight problems print more student blanks than verify.json covers (the expanded forms in 3 and 4 are the declared skill and are unchecked), and the Quick Answers bank prints em-dashes for both compare items.
